title: Risk: five steps, the Agilometer and risk burn-down
blurb: Weave the five risk steps into iterations, read and improve the Agilometer, and use a risk-adjusted backlog and a cumulative risk burn-down.
question: Easterholm's supplier works on fixed-price change requests that take six weeks to quote. In the project initiation workshop, which Agilometer slider should reflect this, and where are the resulting risks recorded?

teach.h: Risk in the rhythm of iterations
teach.body: The risk practice identifies, assesses and controls uncertainty so the project is more likely to succeed. PRINCE2 Agile keeps the five steps (identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate) but fits them into the agile cycle. Identifying risks is a fixed part of every planning session and every team or project retrospective. Implementing responses and communicating them run through the iteration cycles and the feedback loops already in place.

teach.h: The five steps in an agile rhythm

steps.label: Identify
steps.sub: In each planning session and retrospective

teach.caption: Risks can surface anywhere; the planning session and the retrospective are where they are gathered and documented.

teach.body: The Agilometer is a risk product. In the project initiation workshop everyone assesses it, anonymously or in groups, and the results are combined into one project Agilometer. The agile enablement workshop in directing a project reassesses it regularly with the board and agile coaches. Trends appear on the project dashboard and feed the closure lessons. A low slider is a prompt to act: for example, raise flexibility by challenging whether too many requirements are Must haves.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 10.3.2, 10.3.2.3, Tables 13.5 and 13.7

teach.caption: The team sets a likelihood for each tracked risk at its first planning meeting and updates it at each planning session. A falling line shows exposure reducing (10.4.2).

teach.body: In the project initiation workshop, digital staff, social workers and Abacus each score the Agilometer, and the combined result is low on advantageous environmental conditions because Abacus quotes take six weeks. Project manager Simon Archer logs that threat in the risk register. The digital team adds a response story, flagging safeguarding words for urgent review, to its risk-adjusted product backlog. Agile coach Gita Bhatt brings the Agilometer to each agile enablement workshop, and a cumulative risk burn-down shows exposure each sprint.

teach.text: Traps: the Agilometer sits in the risk practice and assesses the risks of agile working; it does not decide change requests or measure progress. The risk management approach holds the procedure; the risk register holds the risks. Risks are identified in every planning session and retrospective, not once at initiation. A cumulative risk burn-down tracks total risk exposure, not remaining work.

items: Five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate, woven into each iteration.
Identify in every planning session and retrospective; implement and communicate in the cycle.
Agilometer: sliders graded low to high; first in project initiation, reassessed in agile enablement.
Challenge Must haves to raise flexibility; contracts that hinder agile lower environmental conditions.
Risk-adjusted backlog = stories plus responses; cumulative risk burn-down = total exposure.

summary: You can now weave the five risk steps into iterations and use the risk management approach, risk register and Agilometer for the right jobs. You can also read and improve Agilometer sliders and apply a risk-adjusted backlog and a cumulative risk burn-down in a scenario.

A.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's project is in the project initiation workshop. Coastline Property Services is paid per job, and any change to how its engineers work must first be agreed with Coastline. Participants score one Agilometer area low because these contract terms would hinder working in an agile way. Which slider is this?
options: Ability to work iteratively and deliver incrementally
A.why: The advantageous environmental conditions slider covers how supportive the working environment is of agile, including contracts that do not inhibit agile ways of working (10.3.2.2).

whyNot.0: Flexibility on what is delivered is about stakeholders' comfort with flexing scope and prioritizing, not contract terms.
whyNot.1: Ease of communication is about how easily the parties communicate, not whether contracts support agile.
whyNot.3: This slider is about whether benefit can be delivered through regular partial deliveries; the contract's terms belong to the environment slider.

A.q: During every sprint planning session and every retrospective, Larkspur Rail's app team spends a few minutes gathering possible threats and opportunities and writing them down. Which step of the risk management technique is the team carrying out?
A.why: In PRINCE2 Agile, identifying risks is a fixed part of every planning session and team or project retrospective, where risks are gathered and documented (10.3.1).

whyNot.1: Assess is where identified risks are estimated and evaluated, after they have been gathered.
whyNot.2: Plan is where risk responses are planned for the risks already identified.
whyNot.3: Implement is where the planned responses are carried out within the iteration cycles.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's e-commerce team adds stories for risk responses, such as extra fraud checks on online payments, into its product backlog next to the feature stories, so that both are prioritized together. Which technique is the team using?
A.why: A risk-adjusted product backlog documents both stories and risk responses in the product backlog (10.4.1).

whyNot.0: A cumulative risk burn-down tracks total risk exposure over iterations; it does not hold stories.
whyNot.1: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working; it is not a backlog of responses.
whyNot.2: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed, not the prioritized responses themselves.

B.q: At its first planning meeting for Release 1, Draycott's software team sets a likelihood for each risk it is tracking, such as the sensor lead time and poor maintenance data. At each later planning session it updates them and plots the total risk level for each sprint. Which technique is this?
B.why: With a cumulative risk burn-down chart the team defines the likelihood of each tracked risk at its first planning meeting and updates it at each planning session, tracking total risk across iterations (10.4.2).

whyNot.0: A burn-down chart shows outstanding work over time, not risk exposure.
whyNot.2: A cumulative flow diagram shows tasks in each workflow state over time, to reveal bottlenecks.
whyNot.3: A risk-adjusted product backlog holds stories and risk responses together; it does not plot total risk.

B.q: Easterholm County Council's Care Online project is in initiation. Project manager Simon Archer needs to set out how risks will be identified and assessed on the project, the scales to be used and who is responsible for what. Where should this be described?
B.why: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed on the project (Table 10.1).

whyNot.0: The risk register records the identified risks and their status, not the procedure for managing them.
whyNot.1: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working; it does not describe the risk procedure.
whyNot.3: The issue management approach covers how issues and changes are handled, not risks.

B.q: Callowmere University's project board wants the Agilometer reassessed regularly during the later stages, with the board, the agile coach and business representatives present, so that agile maturity and the risks to agile adoption stay visible. Which workshop provides for this?
B.why: The agile enablement workshop in directing a project provides regular Agilometer assessments in initiation and later stages for the board, agile coaches and business representatives (Table 13.5).

whyNot.0: The project initiation workshop is where the first combined project Agilometer is created, in initiation.
whyNot.1: The team retrospective reflects on one team's last iteration; it is not a board-level Agilometer review.
whyNot.2: The progress review workshop looks at stage status, dashboard metrics and demos, not regular Agilometer reassessment.

C.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's Agilometer shows a low score for flexibility on what is delivered, because many stakeholders insist every feature is essential. Agile coach Nikhil Rao runs a session with them to challenge whether each Must have, and the assumptions behind it, really deserves that priority. Is this an appropriate application of the risk practice, and why?
options: Yes, because challenging Must haves raises flexibility
Yes, because more collaboration lifts every slider
No, because Must haves are fixed under fix and flex
No, because the Agilometer is reviewed at closure
C.why: The flexibility slider can be improved by checking whether too many requirements are Must haves and challenging the priority or the assumptions behind it (10.3.2.3).

whyNot.1: Collaboration is its own slider; this does not explain how the action improves flexibility on what is delivered.
whyNot.2: Must haves are fixed once agreed, but challenging whether an item truly is a Must have is exactly how flexibility is improved.
whyNot.3: Agilometer trends feed closure lessons, but it is reassessed and acted on throughout the project.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project has started its first delivery stage. Project manager Rhys Pengelly identified risks in initiation and asks the teams not to raise any new risks until the next stage boundary, so that sprints stay focused. Is this an appropriate application of the risk practice, and why?
options: Yes, because stage boundaries confirm that risks are acceptable
Yes, because the risk register was created during initiation
No, because new risks should be raised as issues instead
No, because risks are identified in each planning and retrospective
C.why: Identifying risks is a fixed part of every planning session and team or project retrospective in PRINCE2 Agile; risks can surface at any time (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Stage boundaries do confirm that risks remain acceptable, but that does not justify stopping identification between them.
whyNot.1: The register's creation date does not limit when risks are added; it is updated throughout.
whyNot.2: A risk is an uncertain event; it belongs in the risk register, not the issue register.

C.q: Easterholm County Council has received a request to add text message updates to Release 1. The assistant director proposes that the board use the project's Agilometer to decide whether the request should be accepted. Is this an appropriate application of the risk practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the Agilometer rates flexibility on delivery
Yes, because the board uses it in agile enablement
No, because it assesses the risks of agile working
No, because it is completed by the delivery team
C.why: The Agilometer is a tool to identify and monitor the risks of agile working; change requests are handled through the issues practice (10.3.1, 11.3.2).

whyNot.0: One slider is about flexibility, but the tool assesses agile-working risk, not individual change requests.
whyNot.1: The board does review it in the agile enablement workshop, but that does not make it a change decision tool.
whyNot.3: All participants of the project initiation workshop contribute to it, so this reason is untrue as well as beside the point.

reteach.title: A sailing trip, checked each morning
reteach.question: A skipper takes a small boat along the coast over a week. How does she manage risk day by day, and how does she judge whether the crew is ready for the trip at all?

blocks.h: Daily risk talk and a readiness check
blocks.body: Each morning briefing and each evening debrief, the crew lists new risks: weather, tides, a loose fitting. They size each one, decide a response, act on it during the day and keep everyone told. Before the trip, the skipper also rates how ready the crew is for this kind of sailing: how well they communicate, cooperate and adapt. That readiness check is the Agilometer.

head: Sailing trip
PRINCE2 Agile
rows: Size, respond, act, tell the crew
Total hazard score falling each day

blocks.text: The readiness rating does not decide whether to add an extra harbour stop. That is a change to the plan, handled separately.

explain.body: Identify gathers and documents risks. Assess estimates and evaluates them. Plan chooses responses. Implement carries the responses out within the iterations. Communicate keeps people informed through existing feedback loops.

test.q: Draycott's software team has assessed the threat that Senticore's ten-week sensor lead time could delay Release 2. It now agrees to order the Release 2 sensors during Release 1 as its response. Which step of the risk technique is this?
test.why: The plan step is where the necessary risk responses are planned (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Identify gathers and documents the risk, which has already been done.
whyNot.1: Assess estimates and evaluates the risk, which the team has already done.
whyNot.2: Communicate keeps stakeholders informed; choosing the response is planning.

explain.body: Match the scenario's concern to the slider: contracts and wider support point to environmental conditions; difficulty talking across sites points to ease of communication; reluctance to flex scope points to flexibility on what is delivered.

children.edge: Hard to talk to each other
children.label: Ease of communication

test.q: Callowmere University's wellbeing staff work across two campuses, and many work part-time or remotely, so they often miss face-to-face meetings with the web team. Which Agilometer slider does this MOST directly affect?
test.why: Ease of communication is high when communication is very easy among all parties; split sites and missed meetings lower it (10.3.2.2).

whyNot.0: Flexibility is about stakeholders' comfort with flexing scope, not how easily people communicate.
whyNot.2: Environmental conditions concern overall support for agile, such as contracts, rather than day-to-day communication.
whyNot.3: This slider concerns delivering benefit through regular partial deliveries, not communication between people.

explain.body: The risk management approach says how risk will be managed. The risk register records each identified risk, with its owner, status and history.

test.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's project manager has identified the threat that Coastline's engineers may not use the new parts list, which would leave second visits unchanged. Where should she record this threat, with its owner and status?
test.why: The risk register is the record of identified risks with their status and history (Table 10.1).

whyNot.1: The approach describes how risk is managed; individual risks go in the register.
whyNot.2: The Agilometer rates six areas of agile suitability; it does not hold individual threats.
whyNot.3: The lessons log records lessons learned, not current risks.

explain.body: A cumulative risk burn-down shows total risk exposure across iterations. Ideally it falls; a rising line means exposure is growing and needs attention.

test.q: Draycott's cumulative risk burn-down chart has risen for the last three sprints. What does this MOST LIKELY show?
options: Remaining work in the sprint is growing
A queue is building in one workflow state
test.why: A cumulative risk burn-down tracks the total risk level across iterations; a rising line means exposure is growing (10.4.2).

whyNot.0: Remaining work is shown by a burn-down chart of story points, not a risk burn-down.
whyNot.2: Velocity is the rate of story points delivered, which this chart does not show.
whyNot.3: A queue in a workflow state is shown by a cumulative flow diagram.
